match: IndexError: list index out of range
title: That position does not exist
plain: You asked for a position the list does not have. Positions start at 0, so a list with 4 items only has positions 0 to 3. Asking for position 4 is too far.
fix: Check whether your loop or index goes one step past the end. The last position is len(list) - 1.

match: IndexError: string index out of range
title: That position does not exist in the text
plain: You asked for a letter at a position the text does not have. Positions start at 0 and the last one is len(text) - 1.
fix: Check for an off-by-one: are you using len(text) where you need len(text) - 1.

match: IndexError: pop from empty list
title: Nothing left to remove
plain: You tried to take an item out of a list that has no items.
fix: Check that the list has something in it before you remove from it.

match: NameError: name '(.+)' is not defined
title: Python does not know that name
plain: You used the name {1}, but nothing has stored a value under that name yet. It may be a spelling difference, or you used it before the line that creates it.
fix: Check the spelling and capital letters of {1}, and make sure a line above gives it a value.

match: ^SyntaxError: invalid syntax$
title: Python cannot read this line
plain: The line is not written in a shape Python understands. Common causes: a missing colon at the end of an if, for or def line, a missing bracket or quote mark, or = used where == was meant.
fix: Look at the line named in the message and the line just above it. Count your brackets and quotes.

match: SyntaxError: expected ':'
title: A colon is missing
plain: Lines that start with if, elif, else, for, while or def must end with a colon.
fix: Add : at the end of the line.

match: SyntaxError: '\(' was never closed|SyntaxError: unterminated string literal|SyntaxError: EOL while scanning string literal
title: A bracket or quote mark was opened but not closed
plain: Every opening bracket or quote mark needs a matching closing one.
fix: Count the ( and ), and the quote marks, on the line named.

match: SyntaxError: cannot assign to (.+) here\. Maybe you meant '==' instead of '='
title: You used = where you meant ==
plain: One = means store a value. Inside an if you want to ask a question, which takes two equals signs.
fix: Change = to == in the if line.

match: SyntaxError: invalid syntax\. Maybe you meant '==' or ':=' instead of '='\?
title: You used = where you meant ==
plain: One = means store a value. Inside an if you want to ask a question, which takes two equals signs.
fix: Change = to == in the if line.

match: IndentationError: expected an indented block
title: The lines under this line need to be indented
plain: After a line that ends with a colon, the lines that belong to it must be pushed in by 4 spaces.
fix: Indent the next line by 4 spaces.

match: IndentationError: unexpected indent
title: This line is indented but should not be
plain: The line is pushed in further than the lines around it, and nothing above it asks for that.
fix: Remove the extra spaces at the start of the line.

match: IndentationError: unindent does not match any outer indentation level
title: The spacing at the start of the lines does not line up
plain: Lines that belong together must start in exactly the same column.
fix: Make the indents line up, using 4 spaces for each level.

match: TypeError: can only concatenate str \(not \"int\"\) to str
title: You tried to add text and a number
plain: The + sign can join text to text, or add number to number, but not text to a number.
fix: Turn the number into text with str(...), or turn the text into a number with int(...).

match: TypeError: unsupported operand type\(s\) for (.+): '(\w+)' and '(\w+)'
title: Those two kinds of value do not mix
plain: You tried to use the operator {1} between a {2} and a {3}, and Python does not know how to do that.
fix: Check what each side holds. A common cause is input(), which gives text, not a number. Wrap it with int(...).

match: TypeError: '(\w+)' object is not callable
title: You used round brackets on something that is not a function
plain: Round brackets after a name mean run it as a function. The name holds a {1}, which cannot be run.
fix: Check that you did not give a variable the same name as a function, such as sum or list.

match: TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not (\w+)
title: A position must be a whole number
plain: You used a {1} between the square brackets. Positions have to be whole numbers.
fix: Use int(...) to turn text into a whole number, or use // instead of / when dividing.

match: TypeError: string indices must be integers
title: A position must be a whole number
plain: You used something that is not a whole number as a position in text.
fix: Check what is between the square brackets. Use int(...) if it came from input().

match: TypeError: '(\w+)' object is not subscriptable
title: You used square brackets on something that has no positions
plain: Square brackets pick an item by position, but a {1} has no positions.
fix: Check that the name holds a list or text, and not a number or None.

match: TypeError: object of type '(\w+)' has no len\(\)
title: len needs something with items inside
plain: len counts items, but a {1} does not hold a row of items.
fix: Check the name holds a list or text. A number has no length.

match: TypeError: (\w+)\(\) takes (\d+) positional arguments? but (\d+) (?:was|were) given
title: Wrong number of inputs to the function
plain: The function {1} expects {2} input(s), but you gave it {3}.
fix: Count the inputs in the def line and the line that uses the function. They must match.

match: TypeError: (\w+)\(\) missing (\d+) required positional argument
title: The function was not given enough inputs
plain: The function {1} needs more inputs than you gave it.
fix: Compare the def line with the line that uses the function.

match: ValueError: invalid literal for int\(\) with base 10: '(.*)'
title: That text is not a whole number
plain: You asked Python to turn '{1}' into a whole number, but it is not one. An empty or spaced-out piece causes this too.
fix: If the line holds several numbers, use .split() first and turn each piece into a number.

match: ValueError: not enough values to unpack
title: Fewer values than names
plain: You tried to split a line into more names than it has pieces.
fix: Check how many values the input line really has.

match: ValueError: too many values to unpack
title: More values than names
plain: You tried to put more values into names than you made names for.
fix: Count the names on the left and the values on the right.

match: ZeroDivisionError
title: Dividing by zero
plain: Dividing by zero has no answer, so Python stops.
fix: Check what the bottom number can be, and handle the zero case with an if.

match: EOFError
title: The program asked for input that was not there
plain: input() tried to read a line, but the typed input had run out. Your code is asking for more lines than the test gives.
fix: Count how many input() calls your code makes and compare with the lines the problem says to expect.

match: AttributeError: '(\w+)' object has no attribute '(\w+)'
title: That kind of value has no such tool
plain: A {1} does not have a tool called {2}. For example, a list has append but a number does not.
fix: Check the spelling of {2} and that the name holds the kind of value you expect.

match: UnboundLocalError: .*'(\w+)'
title: A name was used before it got a value inside a function
plain: Inside the function, {1} is used before any line gives it a value there.
fix: Give {1} a starting value inside the function before you use it.

match: KeyError: (.+)
title: That key is not in the dictionary
plain: You asked a dictionary for {1}, but it has nothing stored under that name.
fix: Check the spelling, or use .get(...) which does not stop when the key is missing.

match: RecursionError
title: A function kept calling itself forever
plain: The function called itself over and over with no way to stop.
fix: Make sure there is a stopping case that returns without calling again.
